title: Market Wars: Brand Territory Showdown
theme: Business Strategy, Market Share & Competitive Expansion
description: Expand your brand across the market grid in a head-to-head battle for market dominance! Place storefronts strategically to claim customer territory while your rival does the same. Every move teaches real business concepts — from market share and competitive positioning to brand loyalty and expansion timing.
learning_objectives: Understand market share dynamics and how brands compete for customer territory
Learn competitive positioning: when to expand aggressively vs. defend existing markets
Practice strategic timing — knowing when to enter a new market segment
Explore the concept of brand moats and how surrounding territory creates loyalty barriers
Develop skills in reading competitor moves and adapting your expansion strategy
Understand opportunity cost and resource allocation in business growth
how_to_play: You and the AI take turns placing brand outlets on a 9x9 market grid. You place Your Brand storefronts; the AI places Rival Brand locations.
Surround empty intersections with your brand to claim that customer territory — these consumers become loyal to your brand.
If you completely surround a cluster of Rival Brand locations (no empty adjacent spaces), those locations close — you've driven the competition out!
The Ko rule prevents you from immediately reclaiming a market you just lost, simulating the time it takes to rebuild brand presence.
The game ends when both players pass consecutively, indicating the market has reached saturation.
Your score is loyal customer territory plus competitor locations you shut down. The rival gets a 6.5 point komi advantage for being the established brand. Dominate the market to win!

storybook_pages.title: A Market Ripe for Disruption
storybook_pages.text: You're the founder of a rising brand entering a competitive market. An established rival already has momentum, but the grid is wide open. Every intersection represents a potential customer base — a neighborhood, a demographic, a market segment. Your mission: expand strategically, claim territory, and build an empire of brand loyalty before your rival locks you out.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: bustling city market grid viewed from above with blue storefronts on one side and orange rival stores on the other, customers walking between them, neon signs, modern business cartoon style

storybook_pages.title: The Art of Expansion
storybook_pages.text: Smart brands don't just open stores everywhere — they think about territory. Surround a market segment and those customers become loyal. Cut off a rival's supply chain and their stores close. But overextend too fast and you leave gaps the competition will exploit. It's not about being everywhere — it's about being in the right places.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: business strategy board showing blue and orange brand territories on a grid, arrows showing expansion and encirclement moves, market share pie charts floating above, sleek modern cartoon style

storybook_pages.title: Market Dominance
storybook_pages.text: As the market fills up, every placement becomes critical. Do you defend your core territory or launch a bold expansion into rival turf? Do you consolidate your gains or try to encircle the competition? The best entrepreneurs know when to hold and when to strike. Your market share is your score — make every storefront count.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: dramatic aerial view of a nearly-full market grid with blue and orange territories interlocking, a scoreboard showing market share percentages, cityscape background, competitive business cartoon style

glossary_terms.definition: The process of selecting among alternatives based on available information and values.
glossary_terms.example: Choosing between two career paths based on income, passion, and long-term growth.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Good decision-making combines rational analysis with awareness of cognitive biases that distort judgment.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Leaders make high-stakes decisions daily — the quality of their process matters as much as the decision itself.

glossary_terms.definition: Analyzing information objectively to form a well-reasoned judgment.
glossary_terms.example: Questioning whether a statistic is representative before using it to make a decision.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Critical thinking involves identifying assumptions, evaluating evidence, and considering alternative perspectives.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Journalists fact-check before publishing; scientists replicate experiments before claiming discoveries.

glossary_terms.definition: The belief that abilities can be developed through effort and learning from failure.
glossary_terms.example: Seeing a poor game result as feedback on what to practice, not evidence of being bad at the game.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Research by Carol Dweck shows people with growth mindsets achieve more and recover better from setbacks.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Students who believe intelligence is fixed give up when challenged; those with growth mindset persist and improve.

cultural_context: India's business landscape is characterised by fierce competition for geographic markets — from telecom to FMCG to e-commerce. Territory strategy in this game mirrors the market expansion decisions faced by Indian companies scaling from metro to Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities.
reflection_prompt: Where did you trade influence for territory? Was it worth it?
